ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High contrast ratio; predominantly low-intensity black background with dense clusters of high-intensity white pixels forming circular and mottled patterns across approximately 40% of the visible surface.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: High-intensity white circular rings and solid spots are distributed across both lobes, with higher density toward the distal tips. The medial area near the notch remains primarily low-intensity black with fewer white pixel clusters.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped central depression with a sharp interior angle. The bisection creates a distinct separation between the left and right lobe structures.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Highly irregular trailing edge characterized by high-frequency, high-amplitude serrations. Peaks and valleys are visible along the entire boundary from the notch to the tips, isolated clearly against the water background.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Strongly convex curvature on the outer trailing edges, tapering toward sharp distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Extensive spatial detection of circular high-contrast white pixel rings (rosettes) ranging in size, densely populated across the entire visible ventral area, suggesting widespread cookie-cutter shark bite scars or barnacle attachment points.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Large, protruding clusters of barnacles are visible on the leading edges of the distal tips of both lobes, creating a jagged, non-organic extension of the fluke's geometry.
other_distinctive_markers: Highly unique 'polka-dot' or ring-scar pattern covering the majority of the visible fluke surface, combined with significant biofouling (barnacle growth) on the tips.
